rows.speaker: العامة
rows.claim: The majority reads the verb with kasra on ḥāʾ and lām, from ḥalla meaning to become due; the cited parallels use the same sense.
rows.anchor: قراءة العامة من حل عليه كذا أي: وجب، من حل الدين يحل أي: وجب قضاؤه

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisāʾī and others read both consonants with ḍamma, deriving the verb from ḥalla meaning to descend.
rows.anchor: وقراءة الكسائي من حل يحل أي: نزل، ومنه

rows.speaker: ابن عتيبة
rows.claim: Ibn ʿUtayba combines the majority’s kasra on ḥāʾ with al-Kisāʾī’s ḍamma on lām.
rows.anchor: وابن عتيبة وافق العامة في الحاء، والكسائي في اللام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prevailing analysis makes “My wrath” the subject of yaḥillu in either reading.
rows.anchor: والمشهور أن فاعل " يحل " في القراءتين هو " غضبي "

rows.speaker: صاحب اللوامح
rows.claim: The author of al-Lawāmiḥ treats “My wrath” as an object, with the subject omitted as obvious and understood as their transgression; he disallows making wrath the subject.
rows.anchor: إنه مفعول به، وإن الفاعل ترك لشهرته، والتقدير: فيحل عليكم طغيانكم غضبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says al-Lawāmiḥ’s account is awkward: if the verb is from iḥlāl, it takes one object, either “My wrath” with transgression as subject or an omitted object with wrath as subject.
rows.anchor: فعنده أن حل متعد بنفسه لأنه من الإحلال كما صرح هو به

rows.speaker: طلحة
rows.claim: Ṭalḥa reads a prohibitive lā with emphatic nūn: do not expose yourselves to transgression lest wrath become due, like lā arīnnaka hāhunā.
rows.anchor: وقرأ طلحة " لا يحلن عليكم " ب " لا " الناهية وكسر الحاء

rows.speaker: زيد بن علي
rows.claim: Zayd ibn ʿAlī reads taṭghaw with ḍamma on ghayn, from ṭaghā yaṭghū, like ghadā yaghdū.
rows.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي " ولا تطغوا " بضم الغين من طغا يطغوا

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ allows yaḥillu to be jussive, coordinated with lā taṭghaw; the author objects that this would wrongly make the verse forbid wrath from descending.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يكون مجزوما عطفا على " لا تطغوا " كذا قال أبو البقاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers an accusative subjunctive with an elided an in the consequence clause, which fits the meaning clearly.
rows.anchor: والثاني: أنه منصوب بإضمار " أن " في الجواب. وهو واضح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The construction hum ulāʾi parallels the wording in 2:85.
rows.anchor: قوله: { هم أولاء على أثري }: كقوله: ثم أنتم هؤلاء تقتلون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase ʿalā atharī may be a second predicate or a circumstantial phrase.
rows.anchor: و " على أثري " يجوز أن يكون خبرا ثانيا، وأن يكون حالا

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority reads ulāʾi with a kasra hamza; al-Ḥasan and Ibn Muʿādh replace the hamza with kasra yāʾ for ease.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور " اولاء " بهمزة مكسورة. والحسن وابن معاذ بياء مكسورة

rows.speaker: ابن وثاب
rows.claim: Ibn Waththāb shortens ulāʾi to ūlā, without the hamza.
rows.anchor: وابن وثاب " أولا " بالقصر دون همزة

rows.speaker: طائفة
rows.claim: A group reads ulāya with open yāʾ, which the author regards as close to an error.
rows.anchor: وقرأت طائفة " أولاي " بياء مفتوحة، وهي قريبة من الغلط

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority reads atharī with fatḥa on hamza and yāʾ; Abū ʿAmr in ʿAbd al-Wārith’s narration and Zayd ibn ʿAlī read kasra hamza and silent yāʾ.
rows.anchor: والجمهور على أثري " بفتح الهمزة، والياء. وأبو عمرو في رواية عبد الوارث

rows.speaker: عيسى
rows.claim: ʿĪsā reads ithrī with ḍamma hamza and silent yāʾ; al-Kisāʾī identifies this form as a dialect.
rows.anchor: وعيسى بضمها وسكون الياء، وحكاها الكسائي لغة

rows.speaker: العامة
rows.claim: The majority reads wa-aḍallahum as a past verb whose subject is al-Sāmirī.
rows.anchor: العامة على أنه فعل ماض مسند إلى السامري

rows.speaker: أبو معاذ
rows.claim: Abū Muʿādh and others read wa-aḍalluhum as a nominative مبتدأ and comparative adjective, with al-Sāmirī as its predicate.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو معاذ في آخرين " وأضلهم " مرفوعا بالابتداء، وهو أفعل تفضيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghaḍbāna and asifan are both circumstantial accusatives; their detailed analysis was given earlier in Sūrat al-Aʿrāf.
rows.anchor: حالان. وقد تقدم تحقيق ذلك في سورة الأعراف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Waʿdan ḥasanan may be an emphatic verbal noun with the second object omitted, understood as scripture and guidance, or omitted for generality; alternatively it means the promised thing as the second object.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يكون مصدرا مؤكدا، والمفعول الثاني محذوف تقديره: يعدكم بالكتاب وبالهداية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In mawʿidī, the verbal noun may be annexed to its subject: “you found me having broken my promise to you.”
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون مضافا لفاعله بمعنى: أوجدتموني أخلفتكم ما وعدتكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, mawʿidī is annexed to its object: they had promised Moses to adhere to his religion and community.
rows.anchor: وأن يكون مضافا لمفعوله، بمعنى: أنهم وعدوه أن يتمسكوا بدينه وشيعته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lā tarā fīhā ʿiwajan may be independent, circumstantial of the mountains, or an adjective of qāʿan or of the second object, depending on the preceding phrase’s parsing.
rows.anchor: يجوز في هذه الجملة أن تكون مستأنفة، وأن تكون حالا من الجبال

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī explains the kasra in ʿiwaj as a precise denial of subtle unevenness detectable only by geometric measurement, so the earth’s quality is treated as conceptual rather than visible.
rows.anchor: فنفي الله تعالى ذلك العوج الذي دق ولطف عن الإدراك، اللهم إلا بالقياس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-amt means a slight rise or irregularity; it is also glossed as a hill, cracks in the ground, or mounds.
rows.anchor: والأمت: النبو اليسير. يقال: مد حبله حتى ما فيه أمت

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One gloss takes al-amt as a hill, close in meaning to a slight rise; other glosses are cracks in the earth or mounds.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الأمت: التل، وهو قريب من الأول. وقيل: الشقوق في الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yawmaʾidhin is accusative with yattabiʿūn; al-Zamakhsharī instead makes it a substitute for yawm al-qiyāma, which the author rejects as too distant and syntactically disconnected.
rows.anchor: قوله: { يومئذ }: منصوب ب " يتبعون ". وقيل: بدل من { يوم القيامة }. قاله الزمخشري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author supplies the temporal sense as “the day when the mountains are flattened.”
rows.anchor: والتقدير: يوم إذ نسفت الجبال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lā ʿiwaja lahu may be independent, circumstantial of al-dāʿī, or an adjective describing an omitted verbal noun for following.
rows.anchor: قوله: { لا عوج له } يجوز أن تكون الجملة مستأنفة، وأن تكون حالا من " الداعي "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in lahu most clearly refers to the caller: everyone hears the call, which does not favor some over others.
rows.anchor: أظهرها: أنه يعود على الداعي أي: لا عوج لدعائه بل يسمع جميعهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other pronoun analyses refer it to the omitted following, or understand a syntactic inversion meaning there is no deviation from the caller for them.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو عائد على ذلك المصدر المحذوف أي لا عوج لذلك الاتباع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamsan is a direct object in a free exception and means a faint sound; other glosses are lip movement without speech or the sound of footsteps, with a cited verse of poetry for the latter.
rows.anchor: والهمس: الصوت الخفي. قيل: هو تحريك الشفتين دون نطق

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī glosses hams as a faint whisper, the same root used for the whispered consonants.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري: " هو الركز الخفي. ومنه الحروف المهموسة "

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another gloss understands hams as the sound of footsteps on earth, supported by an unattributed poetic line about walking with a soft tread.
rows.anchor: ومنه همست الإبل: إذا سمع ذلك من وقع أخفافها على الأرض قال: 3319 وهن يمشين بنا هميسا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yawmaʾidhin may substitute for the prior time phrase or be governed by the verb following lā for grammarians who allow that construction; the sense is the day the caller is followed.
rows.anchor: قوله: { يومئذ }: بدل مما تقدم أو منصوب بما بعد " لا " عند من يجيز ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Illā man udhina may be the object of tanfaʿ, with man denoting the person for whom intercession is made.
rows.anchor: والناصب له " تنفع ". و " من " حينئذ واقعة على المشفوع له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It may instead stand in the nominative as a substitute for al-shafāʿa, with an omitted annexed noun: “except the intercession of one permitted.”
rows.anchor: أنه في محل رفع بدلا من الشفاعة، ولا بد من حذف مضاف تقديره: إلا شفاعة من أذن له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As an exception from intercession with the omitted annexed noun, it is connected; without that estimate it is disconnected, accusative in Hijazi usage or nominative in Tamimi usage.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون استثناء منقطعا إذا لم تقدر شيئا، وحينئذ يجوز أن يكون منصوبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both occurrences of lahu are causal, meaning “for his sake” or “for their sake,” as in 46:11.
rows.anchor: و " له " في الموضعين للتعليل كقوله: وقال الذين كفروا للذين آمنوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Illā raḥmatan may be an object of purpose, “for mercy,” or a circumstantial accusative that hyperbolically makes the Prophet himself mercy; alternatively, an omitted noun or the sense “merciful” is understood.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يكون مفعولا له أي: لأجل الرحمة. ويجوز أن ينتصب على الحال مبالغة

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A Prophetic report calls the Messenger a mercy bestowed upon people.
rows.anchor: في الحديث " يا أيها الناس إنما أنا رحمة مهداة "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lil-ʿālamīn may modify an implied noun as an adjective of mercy, or attach to arsalnāka for grammarians who allow attachment across illā; those who disallow it supply an omitted element.
rows.anchor: قوله: { للعالمين } يجوز أن يتعلق بمحذوف على أنها صفة ل " رحمة " أي: كائنة للعالمين. ويجوز أن يتعلق ب " أرسلناك "

rows.speaker: الشيخ
rows.claim: The Shaykh allows an after-illā phrase to attach to what precedes when the verb is unoccupied by another complement, as in mā marartu illā bi-Zayd.
rows.anchor: أما إذا فرغ فيجوز نحو: ما مررت إلا بزيد، كذا قاله الشيخ هنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author objects that this example is also a free construction: the phrase after illā depends on what precedes it as a complement.
rows.anchor: وفيه نظر من حيث إن هذا أيضا مفرغ؛ لأن المفرغ عبارة عما افتقر ما بعد " إلا " لما قبلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ādhantukum means “I informed you”; the hamza makes the verb transitive.
rows.anchor: قوله: { آذنتكم }: أي: أعلمتكم. فالهمزة فيه للنقل

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī derives ādhana from “to know” and says it commonly functions as a warning; he cites 2:279 and Ibn Ḥulza’s line witnessing ādhantnā.
rows.anchor: آذن منقول من أذن إذا علم، ولكنه كثر استعماله في الجري مجرى الإنذار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAlā sawāʾ is a circumstantial phrase applying to both speaker and hearers: all are equally informed, with nothing concealed from anyone.
rows.anchor: في محل نصب على الحال من الفاعل والمفعول معا، أي: مستوين في العلم

rows.speaker: العامة
rows.claim: The majority leaves the yāʾ in wa-in adrī quiescent, as no other factor requires a vowel.
rows.anchor: العامة على إرسال الياء ساكنة، إذ لا موجب لغير ذلك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbās gives the yāʾ fatḥa in wa-in adrī aqārīb and in the parallel wa-in adrī laʿallahu fitna.
rows.anchor: وروي عن أبن عباس أنه قرأ: " وإن أدري أقريب " ، " وإن أدري لعله فتنة " بفتح الياءين

rows.speaker: ابن مجاهد
rows.claim: Ibn Mujāhid flatly rejects this reading.
rows.anchor: على أن ابن مجاهد أنكر هذه القراءة البتة

rows.speaker: ابن جني
rows.claim: Ibn Jinnī calls the reading erroneous because in this context inna is negative and does not govern the yāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن جني: " هو غلط، لأن " إن " نافية لا عمل لها "

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ relays an elaborate account in which hamza’s vowel shifts to yāʾ, then the hamza is replaced and restored to avoid beginning with a consonant cluster.
rows.anchor: ونقل أبو البقاء عن غيره أنه قال في تخريجها: " إنه ألقى حركة الهمزة على الياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author calls that account needlessly contrived; it does not explain the second instance, and he prefers treating the transmitter as mistaken and the reading as aberrant.
rows.anchor: وهذا تخريج متكلف لا حاجة إليه. ونسبة راويها عن ابن عباس إلى الغلط أولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interrogative clause is the object of adrī, suspending its government; the delayed queried phrase preserves the verse ending, since it would otherwise follow aqārīb directly.
rows.anchor: والجملة الاستفهامية في محل نصب ب " أدري " لأنها معلقة لها عن العمل، وأخر المستفهم عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mā tūʿadūn may be a subject with aqārīb/am baʿīd as predicates; Abū al-Baqāʾ allows either adjective to govern it as subject, a case of syntactic competition because both fit semantically.
rows.anchor: قلت: يعني أنه يجوز أن تكون المسألة من التنازع فإن كلا من الوصفين يصح تسلطه على " ما توعدون "

rows.speaker: حفص
rows.claim: Ḥafṣ reads qāla as a statement by the Messenger; the other readers have the imperative qul.
rows.anchor: قرأ حفص " قال " خبرا عن الرسول عليه السلام. الباقون " قل " على الأمر

rows.speaker: العامة
rows.claim: The majority reads rabb with kasra, omitting the yāʾ of first-person annexation; the author calls this standard Arabic.
rows.anchor: وقرأ العامة " رب " بكسر الباء اجتراء بالكسرة عن ياء الإضافة، وهي الفصحى

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abū Jaʿfar reads rabb with ḍamma; al-Lawāmiḥ calls it a standalone vocative, but the author says it is a recognized dialect of an annexed vocative with the first-person yāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر بضم الباء، فقال صاحب " اللوامح ": " إنه منادى مفرد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects the standalone-vocative analysis and says the omission belongs to an attested dialect of a noun annexed to the speaker’s yāʾ in address.
rows.anchor: قلت: ليس هذا من المنادى المفرد، بل نص بعضهم على أن هذه بعض اللغات الجائزة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, ʿIkrima, and Ibn Yaʿmur read rabbī with a silent yāʾ and aḥkamu as a comparative; the two words are subject and predicate.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس وعكرمة وابن يعمر " ربي " بسكون الياء " أحكم " أفعل تفضيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aḥkamu is also read with fatḥa on mīm as a past verb, serving as predicate of rabbī.
rows.anchor: وقرىء " أحكم " بفتح الميم كألزم، على أنه فعل ماض في محل خبر

rows.speaker: العامة
rows.claim: The majority reads taṣifūn in direct address; the Messenger read yaṣifūn to Ubayy, and that version is also reported from ʿĀṣim and Ibn ʿĀmir.
rows.anchor: وقرأ العامة " تصفون " بالخطاب. وقرأ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم على أبي رضي الله عنه " يصفون "

rows.speaker: الأخوان
rows.claim: The two readers read mansakan with kasra here and in the next occurrence; the rest read it with fatḥa.
rows.anchor: قرأ الأخوان هذا وما بعده " منسكا " بالكسر، والباقون بالفتح

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view treats the two forms as synonymous, meaning either the place or the act of ritual sacrifice; another assigns place to kasra and verbal noun to fatḥa.
rows.anchor: فقيل: هما بمعنى واحد. والمراد بالمنسك مكان النسك أو المصدر. وقيل: المكسور مكان

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls the kasra anomalous and not analogically licensed, suggesting al-Kisāʾī may have heard it from Arabs.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية: " والكسر في هذا من الشاذ، ولا يسوغ فيه القياس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author objects that al-Kisāʾī transmitted a Qurʾānic reading, so need not rely on a conjectured hearing; “anomalous” means non-analogical, while usage is eloquent and the pattern’s regular form is fatḥa.
rows.anchor: قلت: وهذا الكلام منه غير مرضي: كيف يقول: ويشبه أن يكن الكسائي سمعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers reading al-budna in the accusative by the construction of الاشتغال, even though it requires an implied verb, because a verbal clause precedes; an alternative reads it nominative as subject.
rows.anchor: العامة على نصب " البدن " على الاشتغال. ورجح النصب وإن كان محوجا لإضمار

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Most readers have a silent dāl; al-Ḥasan and narrations from Nāfiʿ and Abū Jaʿfar’s shaykha have ḍamma, with both forms analyzed as plurals of badana.
rows.anchor: والعامة أيضا على تسكين الدال. وقرأ الحسن وتروى نافع وشيخة أبي جعفر بضمها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The silent dāl may be an original form or a lightened ḍamma; alternative morphology derives budn/badan as plurals of badan or badana, while another treats budn as a singular collective noun.
rows.anchor: فالتسكين يحتمل أن يكون تخفيفا من المضموم، وأن يكون أصلا. وقيل: البدن والبدن جمع بدن

rows.speaker: ابن أبي إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Abī Isḥāq reads al-budunn with ḍamma on both opening consonants and a doubled nūn; it may reflect a weakened final consonant extended from pause, or a form on the pattern fuʿul.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي إسحاق " البدن " بضم الباء والدال وتشديد النون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Badana is named because the animal grows stout.
rows.anchor: وسميت البدنة بدنة لأنها تبدن أي: تسمن

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority restricts budn to camels; al-Zamakhsharī says the name reflects their large bodies and cites the Prophetic rule of one camel or cow for seven, making both legally included for Abū Ḥanīfa and his companions though the verse denotes camels.
rows.anchor: الجمهور على ذلك. قال الزمخشري: " والبدن: جمع بدنة سميت لعظم بدنها

rows.speaker: الليث
rows.claim: Al-Layth uses badana broadly for camels, cows, and bulls eligible for sacrifice, but not sheep.
rows.anchor: فقال الليث: البدنة بالهاء تقع على الناقة والبقرة والبعير وما يجوز في الهدي

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: ʿAṭāʾ and others define it as a camel or cow marked for sacrifice.
rows.anchor: وقال عطاء وغيره: ما أشعر من ناقة أو بقرة

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Others restrict budn to mature camels and cattle; the same word can describe a stout man and is a singular collective noun.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون: البدن يراد به العظيم السن من الإبل والبقر. ويقال للسمين من الرجال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min shaʿāʾir Allāh is the second object of jaʿalnā with the sense “made them into.”
rows.anchor: قوله: { من شعائر الله } هو المفعول الثاني للجعل بمعنى التصيير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lakum fīhā khayr is circumstantial, either of the pronoun in jaʿalnāhā or of shaʿāʾir Allāh, depending on whether fīhā refers to the sacrificial camels or the rites; the first is the majority view.
rows.anchor: الجملة حال: إما من " ها " " جعلناها " ، وإما من شعائر الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣawāffa is a circumstantial accusative meaning the animals stand aligned side by side.
rows.anchor: قوله: { صواف } نصب على الحال أي: مصطفة جنب بعضها إلى بعض

rows.speaker: أبو موسى الأشعري
rows.claim: Abū Mūsā, al-Ḥasan, Mujāhid, and Zayd ibn Aslam read ṣawāfī, “purely devoted” to God.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو موسى الأشعري والحسن ومجاهد وزيد بن أسلم " صوافي " جمع صافية

rows.speaker: عمرو بن عبيد
rows.claim: ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd reads ṣawāfiyā with tanwīn on the yāʾ; although this is problematic for a diptote plural, the tanwīn may replace the pause extension vowel or reflect a dialect that declines diptotes.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عمرو بن عبيد كذلك، إلا أنه نون الياء فقرأ " صوافيا "

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī explains tanwīn in ʿAmr’s reading as replacing the lengthened pause vowel, a tanwīn of tarannum.
rows.anchor: ذكره الزمخشري وهو أن يكون التنوين عوضا من حرف الإطلاق عند الوقف

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan also reads ṣawāfin with kasra and tanwīn; its accusative fatḥa is estimated on yāʾ, with deletion and tanwīn like jawārin.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن " صواف " بالكسر والتنوين. وتوجيهها: أنه نصبها بفتحة مقدرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A silent-yāʾ reading ṣawāfī supports estimating the fatḥa on yāʾ; it may either be a true connected form or a pause form carried into connection.
rows.anchor: ويدل على ذلك قراءة بعضهم " صوافي " بياء ساكنة من غير تنوين

rows.speaker: العبادلة
rows.claim: The ʿAbādila, Mujāhid, and al-Aʿmash read ṣawāfin, plural of ṣāfinah: an animal standing on three legs and the tip of a fourth; since this is used of horses, its use for camels is metaphorical.
rows.anchor: وقرأ العبادلة ومجاهد والأعمش " صوافن " بالنون جمع " صافنة " وهي التي تقوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wajabat means “fell”: the sun sets and a wall collapses; the ritual duty is called wājib as if it has fallen upon and bound us. Aws ibn Ḥajar’s verse witnesses the sense of a falling mountain.
rows.anchor: والوجوب: السقوط. وجبت الشمس أي: سقطت. ووجب الجدار أي: سقط

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view calls al-qāniʿ the asker and al-muʿtarr the visitor who comes without asking; another reverses the definitions.
rows.anchor: فالقانع: السائل والمعتر: المعترض من غير سؤال. وقال قوم بالعكس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās first defines al-qāniʿ as satisfied with what is given and al-muʿtarr as one who comes without asking.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: القانع: المستغني بما أعطيته، والمعتر: المعترض من غير سؤال

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās also transmits the reverse pairing: al-qāniʿ is self-restrained, while al-muʿtarr is the asker.
rows.anchor: وعنه أيضا: القانع: المتعفف، والمعتر: السائل

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some define qāniʿ as someone content with little, from qaniʿa yaqnaʿu qanāʿatan; Abū al-Baqāʾ distinguishes qanaʿ without alif as “beggar.”
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم: القانع: الراضي بالشيء اليسير. من قنع يقنع قناعة فهو قانع

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī takes al-qāniʿ as a supplicant, deriving it from humility and asking, while al-muʿtarr either comes without asking or asks openly; he also gives contentment as an alternative for qāniʿ.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: " القانع: السائل. من قنعت وكنعت إذا خضعت له. وسألته قنوعا

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another analysis distinguishes the verbal nouns: qanaʿa qanūʿan means to ask, while qanāʿatan means to be content with one’s sufficiency; al-Shammākh’s line uses al-qanūʿ for the asker.
rows.anchor: وفرق بعضهم بين المعنيين بالمصدر فقال: قنع يقنع قنوعا أي سأل، وقناعة أي: تعفف

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: Ibn Qutayba defines al-muʿtarr as one who comes seeking a favor without asking, citing the verbs ʿarrahu and related forms and two poems as evidence.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن قتيبة: " المعتر: المتعرض من غير سؤال.

rows.speaker: أبو رجاء
rows.claim: Abū Rajāʾ reads al-qanʿ without alif: either a shortened qāniʿ, or the distinct noun for a beggar opposed to a contented qāniʿ; al-Zamakhsharī says al-qanʿ means only the contented person.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو رجاء " القنع " دون ألف. وفيها وجهان

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads al-muʿtarī, the active participle of iʿtarā yaʿtarī.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن: " والمعتري " اسم فاعل من اعترى يعتري

rows.speaker: إسماعيل
rows.claim: Ismāʿīl, also reported from Abū Rajāʾ and al-Ḥasan, reads al-muʿatir with kasra on rāʾ, using the vowel in place of the final root letter.
rows.anchor: وقرأ إسماعيل وتروى عن أبي رجاء والحسن أيضا " والمعتر " بكسر الراء

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ says the reading al-muʿtarī with open yāʾ has the same meaning as the majority’s al-muʿtarr.
rows.anchor: قال أبو البقاء: " وهو في معناه " أي: في معنى " المعتر " في قراءة العامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The kāf in kadhālika sakhkharnāhā is an adjective of an implied verbal noun or a circumstantial phrase describing that noun.
rows.anchor: و[قوله:] { كذلك سخرناها } الكاف نعت مصدر أ و حال من ذلك المصدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bashar can denote one, two, or a group, masculine or feminine; it can also agree in number, as it does here, and in the example from 3:47.
rows.anchor: قوله: { لبشرين }: " بشر " يقع على الواحد والمثنى والمجموع والمذكر والمؤنث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mathalun remains singular and masculine because it behaves like a verbal noun, though it can agree with dual or plural referents, as in 3:13 and 47:38.
rows.anchor: وأما إفراد " مثلنا " فلأنه يجري مجرى المصادر في الإفراد والتذكير

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One explanation is that the intended likeness concerns being human, not number; another says the single form stands for two.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أريد المماثلة في البشرية لا الكمية. وقيل: اكتفي بالواحد عن الاثنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wa-qawhumā lanā ʿābidūn is a circumstantial clause.
rows.anchor: قوله: { وقومهما لنا عابدون } جملة حالية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The time phrase yawma tashhadu is governed by the underlying predicate to which lahum attaches; another view makes ʿadhāb its governor, objected to because ʿadhāb is a qualified verbal noun, though temporal expressions permit this usage.
rows.anchor: قوله: { يوم تشهد }: ناصبه الاستقرار الذي تعلق به " لهم ". وقيل: بل ناصبه " عذاب "

rows.speaker: الأخوان
rows.claim: The two readers use masculine yashhadu because feminine marking is nonliteral and the subject is separated from the verb.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأخوان " يشهد " بالياء من تحت؛ لأن التأنيث مجازي، وقد وقع الفصل

rows.speaker: الباقون
rows.claim: The rest retain feminine tashhadu, matching the grammatical form of the subject.
rows.anchor: والباقون بالتاء مراعاة للفظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tanwīn in idhin substitutes for a clause, expanded as “the day when it testifies”; the author notes an earlier disagreement from al-Akhfash.
rows.anchor: والتنوين في " إذ " عوض من الجملة، تقديره: يوم إذ تشهد. وقد تقدم خلاف الأخفش فيه

rows.speaker: زيد بن علي
rows.claim: Zayd ibn ʿAlī reads yuwaffīhim with lightening, from awfā.
rows.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي " يوفيهم " مخففا من أوفى

rows.speaker: العامة
rows.claim: The majority reads al-ḥaqqa in the accusative as an adjective of dīnahum; Abū Ḥaywa, Abū Rawq, Mujāhid, and Ibn Masʿūd read it nominative as an adjective of God.
rows.anchor: وقرأ العامة بنصب " الحق " نعتا ل " دينهم " ، وأبو حيوة وأبو روق ومجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The time phrase yawma tashaqququ may be governed by an implied “remember,” or by yanfardu Allāhu bi-l-mulk, inferred from 25:26.
rows.anchor: قوله: { ويوم تشقق }: العامل في " يوم ": إما اذكر، وإما: ينفرد الله بالملك يوم تشقق

rows.speaker: الكوفيون
rows.claim: The Kūfans and Abū ʿAmr read tashaqququ here and in Sūrat Qāf with a light form; the rest use gemination, either deleting a tāʾ or assimilating it into shīn.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الكوفيون وأبو عمرو هنا وفي ق " تشقق " بالتخفيف. والباقون بالتشديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two pronunciations reflect deletion by the first group or assimilation of the form’s tāʾ into shīn by the rest, like the two forms of taẓāharūn in al-Baqara.
rows.anchor: والباقون أدغموا تاء التفعل في الشين لما بينهما من المقاربة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bāʾ in bi-l-ghamām may express cause, accompaniment, or the sense “from/about,” supported by examples from 73:18 and 50:44.
rows.anchor: في هذه الباء ثلاثة أوجه، أحدها: على السببية أي: بسبب الغمام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One parsing makes al-mulku the subject, al-ḥaqqu its predicate, and yawmaʾidhin attached to al-mulk; li-l-Raḥmān may attach to al-ḥaqq or be an explanatory phrase or its adjective.
rows.anchor: أن يكون " الملك " مبتدأ، والخبر: " الحق " ، و " يومئذ " متعلق بالملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second parsing makes yawmaʾidhin the predicate, with al-ḥaqqu an adjective of al-mulk; li-l-Raḥmān is parsed as above.
rows.anchor: الثاني: أن الخبر " يومئذ " ، و " الحق " نعت للملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third parsing makes li-l-Raḥmān the predicate, attaches yawmaʾidhin to al-mulk, and treats al-ḥaqqu as an adjective of al-mulk.
rows.anchor: الثالث: أن الخبر " للرحمن " و " يومئذ " متعلق بالملك، و " الحق " نعت للملك

rows.speaker: الأخوان
rows.claim: The two readers have yaʾ in yaʾmurunā, referring to Muhammad; the rest use second-person tāʾ, “what you command us.”
rows.anchor: قرأ الأخوان " يأمرنا " بياء الغيبة يعني محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم. والباقون بالخطاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mā may be a relative pronoun with an omitted resumptive, since amara takes a second object without a preposition.
rows.anchor: و " ما " يجوز أن تكون بمعنى الذي. والعائد محذوف؛ لأنه متصل

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ proposes a stepwise derivation from “command us to prostrate to Him” to the shorter wording.
rows.anchor: ولا حاجة إلى التدريج الذي ذكره أبو البقاء: وهو أن الأصل: لما تأمرنا بالسجود له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says this derivation is not Sibawayh’s doctrine; Sibawayh permits deletion without such intermediate steps.
rows.anchor: قلت: وهذا ليس مذهب سيبويه. ويجوز أن تكون موصوفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mā may instead be a descriptive expression, with its resumptive treated as in the relative analysis.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون موصوفة، والكلام في عائدها موصوفة كهي موصولة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mā may also be a verbal noun with a causal lām: “shall we prostrate because of your command?”; then the object of prostration is omitted and mā does not refer to the object of worship.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون مصدرية، وتكون اللام للعلة أي: أنسجد من أجل أمرك

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī makes the clause at the end of the sūra the predicate of ʿibādu al-Raḥmān, with “those who walk” and following clauses as adjectives of the subject.
rows.anchor: وبه بدأ الزمخشري. " والذين يمشون " وما بعده صفات للمبتدأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative makes yamshūn the predicate of ʿibādu al-Raḥmān.
rows.anchor: والثاني: أن الخبر " يمشون "

rows.speaker: اليماني
rows.claim: Al-Yamānī reads ʿubādu with ḍamma on ʿayn and doubled bāʾ, as a plural of ʿābid; al-Ḥasan reads ʿubud with two ḍammas.
rows.anchor: واليماني " عباد " بضم العين، وشد الباء جمع عابد. والحسن " عبد " بضمتين

rows.speaker: العامة
rows.claim: The majority reads yamshūn as an active verb; al-Yamānī and al-Sulamī read it passive.
rows.anchor: والعامة " يمشون " بالتخفيف مبنيا للفاعل. واليماني والسلمي بالتشديد مبنيا للمفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hawnan is either an adjective of an implied verbal noun (“gentle walking”) or a circumstantial accusative (“gentle”), and hawn means softness and gentleness.
rows.anchor: قوله: { هونا }: إما نعت مصدر أي: مشيا هونا، وإما حال أي: هينين. والهون: اللين والرفق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Salāman may be a cognate accusative after an implied “we greet,” or a direct object meaning they said the word itself; the author also describes it as a safe, upright response that avoids harm.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن ينتصب على المصدر بفعل مقدر أي: نسلم سلاما

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī interprets their words as sound speech that protects them from harm, greeting the ignorant’s foolishness with peace; a cited poem models the response.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري: أي قالوا سدادا من القول يسلمون فيه من الأذى

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh prefers salām to mean safety rather than a greeting: believers were not commanded to greet disbelievers but to make peace, a command later abrogated; he mentions abrogation only for this verse in his book.
rows.anchor: ورجح سيبويه أن المراد بالسلام السلامة لا التسليم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author cites a poem about not answering another’s ignorance with ignorance as evidence for their safe response.
rows.anchor: فنجهل فوق جهل الجاهلينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular rasūl may be a verbal noun meaning “message,” which is singular by nature; the cited poem uses rasūl with this sense.
rows.anchor: إما لأنه مصدر بمعنى رسالة، والمصدر يوحد. ومن مجيء " رسول " بمعنى رسالة قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rasūl may be singular because Moses and Aaron share one law and are treated as one messenger, or because each individually is a messenger.
rows.anchor: وإما لأنهما ذوا شريعة واحدة فنزلا منزلة رسول، وإما لأن المعنى: أن كل واحد منا رسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the singular may stand for dual because Moses and Aaron are inseparable like two eyes or hands; where these explanations do not apply, the wording agrees in dual form at 20:47.
rows.anchor: وحيث لم يقصد هذه المعاني طابق في قوله: إنا رسولا ربك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Walīdan is a circumstantial accusative of the object of nurabbika; it is on the faʿīl pattern with passive sense, naming the boy for what he once was.
rows.anchor: قوله: { وليدا }: حال من مفعول " نربك " وهو فعيل بمعنى مفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min ʿumrika is a circumstantial phrase modifying sinīna.
rows.anchor: قوله: { من عمرك } حال من " سنين "

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: In one narration Abū ʿAmr gives ʿumr a silent mīm as a lightened pronunciation.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو في رواية بسكون الميم تخفيفا
